issues.legal_issue: An agreement presented as a transfer of business-management rights constitutes subletting when its terms and the parties’ conduct show that the tenant transferred the business together with the right to occupy the leased premises.
material_facts: The tenant had leased premises for a hotel and entered into an agreement allowing another person to operate the hotel.

Although the agreement described the arrangement as management of the business and stated that the tenant retained the lease, the operator could run the hotel on his own account, control its staff, and bear its expenses and liabilities.
The operator was required to pay the tenant an amount that included the difference between the existing rent and any increased rent, and he bore the practical burden of paying rent for the premises.
The agreement permitted renewal for further periods and required the operator to undertake repairs to the premises.
The operator was treated in practice as the proprietor of the hotel, controlled the business, and was not required to account to the tenant for its profits or losses.
The landlord obtained an eviction order on the ground of subletting, which was upheld by the appellate authority and the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was a transfer of the hotel business together with the tenant’s interest in the leased premises, and therefore amounted to subletting. The eviction order was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, the substance of the transaction and the parties’ conduct determine whether the tenant has sublet the premises; labels or clauses denying subletting do not control where the arrangement in fact transfers the right to occupy. The Court relied on Bhagwan Das v. S. Rajeev Singh and M. Rodgers v. N. Prakash Rao Naidu, and distinguished Md. Salim v. Md. Ali on its facts. It explained that Dwarka Prasad v. Dwarka Das Saraf concerned the dominant-purpose test for a composite lease and did not require that test to be applied to a purported transfer of hotel-management rights.

rule.if: appeal_against_subletting_eviction and (operator_controls_business_on_own_account and operator_bears_premises_costs and operator_is_recognized_as_proprietor) and (tenant_passes_rent_burden_to_operator or arrangement_allows_continuing_occupation)

predicates.appeal_against_subletting_eviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an eviction order based on alleged subletting by a tenant.
predicates.operator_controls_business_on_own_accoun: The tenant allows another person to control and operate the business on that person’s own account and responsibility.
predicates.operator_bears_premises_costs: The person operating the business bears rent-related costs or other expenses associated with the premises.
predicates.operator_is_recognized_as_proprietor: The person operating the business is treated in practice as its proprietor rather than merely as its manager.
predicates.tenant_passes_rent_burden_to_operator: The tenant makes the operator bear, directly or indirectly, the burden of paying rent for the premises.
predicates.arrangement_allows_continuing_occupation: The arrangement gives the operator the ability to continue occupying the premises beyond a short, fixed operating period.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an eviction order for subletting and the operator controls the business on their own account, bears premises costs, and is recognized as proprietor, the tenant has sublet the premises if the tenant also passes on the rent burden or the arrangement allows continuing occupation.

issues.legal_issue: The operator’s departure from the premises and return of the business to the tenant after subletting has occurred does not defeat the landlord’s right to eviction on that ground.
material_facts: The courts had found that the tenant sublet the premises to the person who operated the hotel.
During the appeal, it was represented that the operator had vacated the premises and returned the business to the tenant, who was again running the hotel through his son.
issues.conclusion: The later change in circumstances did not affect the landlord’s right to evict the tenant on the established ground of subletting.
issues.legal_principle: Where subletting has been established as the ground for eviction under Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, a subsequent return of the business and premises to the tenant does not remove the landlord’s right to eviction. The Court cited no earlier case for this point.

predicates.appeal_against_subletting_eviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an eviction order based on alleged subletting by a tenant.
predicates.subletting_previously_established: The courts have found that the tenant sublet the premises to another person.
predicates.operator_later_vacates_and_returns_busin: After the subletting, the operator vacates the premises and returns the business to the tenant.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges an eviction for subletting, subletting has already been established, and the operator later vacates and returns the business, the landlord retains the right to evict.
